chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Washa, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
Every intoxicant is prohibited, and every fermented drink is prohibited, and Al-Fuqqa' is prohibited.

key_terms.الْفُقَّاعُ: Al-Fuqqa'; a specific type of fermented drink mentioned in the text
key_terms.مُخَمَّرٍ: Fermented; referring to drinks produced through fermentation
key_terms.مُسْكِرٍ: Intoxicant; a substance that causes intoxication

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fermented drinks and intoxicants in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the scope of khamr by distinguishing between general intoxicants and specific fermented beverages like Al-Fuqqa' (a type of beer or fermented drink). It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the prohibition extends beyond wine to any substance causing intoxication, reinforcing the concept of 'ta'abbudi' (divine command) in dietary laws. The mention of Al-Fuqqa' highlights historical context regarding common fermented drinks of the era, ensuring no loophole existed for non-grape fermented beverages.
